pages.text: The Big Bang alone cannot explain why opposite sides of the sky have the same temperature to one part in 100,000: they were never in contact. $(thing)Inflation$() does: before the hot Big Bang, a scalar field - the inflaton - sat high on its potential and made space grow exponentially, sixty e-folds in 10⁻³² s.

Build the $(item)Inflation Chamber$(). It condenses the $(fluid)Inflaton Field$() and $(fluid)False Vacuum$() into $(item)Inflaton Condensate$(). In its Operation console keep the slow-roll ε = 2/φ² below 1 and N = (φ₀² − 2)/4 above 50 - but start the field too high and inflation turns $(thing)eternal$(): quantum jumps outrun the roll, and the bubble never ends (in our universe, other bubbles still may).

$(thing)Reheating$(): at the bottom of its potential the inflaton oscillates and decays. The chamber turns Condensate and a little quark-gluon plasma into $(fluid)Reheating Plasma$() - every particle there is, at 10⁹ GeV and more. That plasma is the raw stuff of every other Origin material.
